title: Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR): Surgical Masterclass, Pearls & Pitfalls
summary: An authoritative, textbook-grade surgical guide detailing surgical anatomy, external vs. endoscopic DCR techniques, step-by-step algorithms, high-yield surgical tricks, and strategies to prevent and manage critical complications.

sections.title: Clinical Overview & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) is the gold-standard surgical bypass procedure designed to reconstruct tear drainage by creating a direct mucosal-lined fistula between the lacrimal sac and the nasal cavity (middle meatus). The primary indication is nasolacrimal duct obstruction (NLDO), most commonly Primary Acquired Nasolacrimal Duct Obstruction (PANDOL). PANDOL is characterized by age-related inflammatory fibrosis and clinicopathologic stenosis of the NLD. Secondary causes include trauma (naso-orbito-ethmoid fractures), dacryolithiasis, granulomatous inflammation (GPA, Sarcoidosis), and neoplasia. Successful surgery hinges on constructing a wide bony osteotomy (≥ 12–15 mm) and tension-free mucosal flap anastomosis.

branches: Anterior Boundary: Frontal process of maxilla (Thick bone)
Posterior Boundary: Lacrimal bone (Thin paper-like bone)
Suture Line: Maxillolacrimal suture (Divides fossa vertically)
Vascular Hazard: Angular Vein (8-10 mm medial to medial canthus)
Intranasal Landmark: Axilla of Middle Turbinate (Corresponds to upper sac)

rows: Probing & Irrigation
23G cannula passed into punctum and canaliculus into lacrimal fossa

HARD STOP = Bone contact (NLD block; ideal DCR candidate).
SOFT STOP = Spongy feel (Canalicular/Common canalicular stenosis).
Dye Disappearance Test (DDT)
Instill 2% fluorescein in inferior fornix; observe at 5 minutes
Persistent dye reservoir indicates functional or anatomical outflow failure.
Jones I (Primary Test)
Instill dye in eye; soft cotton bud under inferior turbinate at 5 min

POSITIVE = Dye retrieved (Patent system).
NEGATIVE = Functional or anatomic block.
Jones II (Secondary Test)
Irrigate lacrimal system after negative Jones I test

DYE RETRIEVED = Functional NLD block.
NO DYE / CLEAR SALINE = Punctal/canalicular block.
Nasal Endoscopy
Rigid 0°/30° endoscope exam of nasal cavity
Identifies septal deviation, middle turbinate hypertrophy, nasal polyps, tumors.
CT / Dacryocystography (DCG)
High-resolution axial/coronal CT or contrast radiography
Mandatory for previous trauma, suspected tumors, facial anomalies, or revision DCR.

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis of Lacrimal Drainage Obstruction

rows: PANDOL
Epiphora, chronic mucopurulent discharge, pain-free swelling below MPL
Hard stop on probing; non-tender mass below MPL; female predilection.
Lacrimal Sac Tumor
Hard, painless mass ABOVE medial palpebral ligament (MPL), bloody epiphora
CT bone erosion; solid mass on imaging; distension above MPL.
Canaliculitis
Punctal pouting, sulfur granules ('sulfur plugs'), medial lid erythema
Actinomyces israelii infection; soft stop; yellow cheesy material expressed.
Dacryolithiasis
Intermittent lacrimal outflow obstruction, fluctuating sac enlargement
Mouldable cast or palpable firm intra-sac calculus during surgical opening.
Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis
Bilateral bloody nasal discharge, saddle nose, refractory dacryocystitis
Positive c-ANCA/PR3; widespread nasal mucosal ulceration/granulomas.

sections.title: Step-by-Step External DCR Technique
content: Step 1: Infiltration & Decongestion — Infiltrate 2% Lidocaine with 1:100,000 Epinephrine along incision and medial canthus; pack nasal cavity with 4% Cocaine or Oxymetazoline 0.05% soaked neurosurgical patties.
Step 2: Skin Incision — 10–12 mm vertical curvilinear incision, 3–5 mm medial to inner canthus (to avoid angular vein and prevent web formation).
Step 3: Periosteal Elevation — Dissect through orbicularis to periosteum; elevate periosteum off frontal process of maxilla to expose anterior lacrimal crest and sac fossa.
Step 4: Osteotomy Creation — Enter lacrimal bone (thin) with Freer elevator/drill; expand bony window to 12–15 mm using Kerrison Rongeur, removing thick frontal process of maxilla.
Step 5: Sac & Nasal Mucosal Flap Creation — Probe canaliculi to tent sac; cut anterior and posterior flaps in 'H' or 'U' shape in both lacrimal sac and opposing nasal mucosa.
Step 6: Antimetabolite Application (Optional) — Apply Mitomycin C (0.2–0.4 mg/mL) soaked sponge onto bony osteotomy edges for 2–3 minutes; rinse copiously with saline.
Step 7: Bicanalicular Stenting — Pass Crawford or Ritleng silicone stents through upper and lower puncta into nasal cavity; tie in nasal cavity with 4-0 silk or silicone clip.
Step 8: Flap Anastomosis & Closure — Suture anterior mucosal flaps with 6-0 Vicryl; close orbicularis layer with 6-0 Vicryl and skin with 6-0 Fast Gut or Monocryl.

sections.title: External DCR vs. Endoscopic Endonasal DCR (E-DCR)

rows: Surgical Approach
Transcutaneous anterior approach via medial canthal incision
Transnasal approach using 0°/30° rigid nasal endoscopes
Skin Scar
Present (3-5 mm medial to canthus); minimal if well-placed
Zero cutaneous incision; no cutaneous scarring
Success Rate
90% – 95% primary success rate
85% – 92% (comparable with experience & powered drills)
Medial Canthal Anatomy
Disrupts Medial Palpebral Ligament (MPL) anterior limb
Preserves Medial Palpebral Ligament and orbicularis pump
Operative Hemostasis
Easier direct pressure & bipolar cautery control
Requires meticulous intranasal packing & suction cautery
Concurrent Pathology
Can perform tissue biopsy / lacrimal sac reconstruction
Ideal for simultaneous septoplasty or middle turbinate surgery

sections.title: High-Yield Surgical Pearls & Tricks
content: Osteotomy Size Rule: 'Big Bone Window = Big Success'. Ensure osteotomy is at least 15x10 mm; extend osteotomy anteriorly past the anterior lacrimal crest and superiorly to the axilla of middle turbinate.
Prevent 'Sump Syndrome': Ensure the bottom of the lacrimal sac and osteotomy extends flush down to the NLD entrance so tears don't pool in a dependent dead-space pouch.
Angular Vein Avoidance: Place skin incision 3-5 mm medial to canthus; angular vein lies 8-10 mm medial. Use blunt dissection once through skin.
Flap Tension Reduction: Make longitudinal incisions on sac and nasal mucosa equal in length; ensure anterior flap flaps drape easily without longitudinal stretch.
MMC Dosage Precision: Apply MMC 0.2 mg/mL for 2-3 mins in patients with severe scarring, revision cases, or tiny narrow lacrimal sacs.

sections.title: Critical Surgical Pitfalls & Prevention
content: Inadequate Superior Osteotomy: Failure to remove bone above the axilla of the middle turbinate leads to scarring of the upper sac flap and high failure rates.
Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) Leak: Superior/posterior entry near the cribriform plate/ethmoid roof. Prevention: Stay below cribriform plate height (insertion of middle turbinate).
Webbing / Bowstring Scar: Incision placed too close to the medial canthal web. Solution: Keep incision straight or slightly curvilinear along natural skin tension lines.
Silicone Tube Prolapse: Tube loops out at medial canthus and contacts cornea. Solution: Place a suture or silicone clip around the intranasal tube legs.
Missing Sac Neoplasm: Always biopsy sac wall if mucosal thickening is rubbery, nodular, highly vascular, or if bone destruction is noted.

sections.title: Red Flags & Surgical Emergencies
content: Clear Intraoperative Rhinorrhea: Indicates CSF breach due to ethmoid roof/cribriform plate violation. Immediate repair with mucoperiosteal flap and intrathecal fluorescein evaluation required.
Rapidly Expanding Retrobulbar Hematoma: Caused by injury to anterior ethmoidal artery or deep orbital fat breach. Requires immediate lateral canthotomy & cantholysis.
Atypical Medial Mass Above MPL: High suspicion for Lacrimal Sac Malignancy (Squamous Cell Carcinoma, Transitional Cell Carcinoma). Contraindicates routine DCR; requires urgent tissue biopsy.
Postoperative Severe Epistaxis: Bleeding from angular vein or anterior ethmoidal branches. Requires posterior/anterior nasal packing or endonasal cauterization.

content.explanation:
F = Fossa exposure (Elevate periosteum off lacrimal fossa)
L = Large Osteotomy (≥12-15mm bone removal clearing anterior crest)
A = Anterior & Posterior mucosal flap design (Lacrimal + Nasal)
P = Probe and Bicanalicular Stenting (Avoid tight tension)
S = Suture flaps & Layered Anatomical Closure (Orbicularis then skin)

branches: Osteotomy Closure: Cicatricial granulation / fibrous occlusion (Most Common)
Sump Syndrome: Incomplete excision of inferior sac floor causing pooling
Canalicular Obstruction: Unrecognized common canalicular stenosis or stent trauma
Nasal Adhesions: Synechiae between ostium and Middle Turbinate or Nasal Septum
Malpositioned Osteotomy: Too small (<8 mm) or placed too far posterior/inferior

sections.title: Postoperative Care & Stenting Protocol
content: Immediate Post-Op: Ice compresses to medial canthus for 48 hours; head elevation 30-45 degrees.
Topical Therapy: Antibiotic-steroid combination drops (e.g., Tobramycin/Dexamethasone) QID for 2 weeks.
Intranasal Therapy: Nasal steroid spray (Fluticasone/Mometasone) BID + Normal Saline nasal sprays QID for 4-6 weeks.
Avoidance Protocol: Strict instruction: NO nose blowing for 10-14 days to prevent subcutaneous emphysema.
Stent Removal: Bicanalicular silicone tubes removed in office at 6 to 12 weeks postoperatively.

sections.title: Pediatric & Special Population Considerations
sections.content: In pediatric populations, congenital NLDO (Hasner membrane persistence) resolves spontaneously in >90% by age 1. Probing, balloon dacryoplasty, and silicone intubation precede DCR. Pediatric DCR is reserved for refractory cases after age 3-4 years. Anatomical considerations in children include smaller facial bones, highly vascularized tissues, and rapid bone re-growth/osteogenesis, making intraoperative MMC (0.2 mg/mL for 2 mins) and meticulous flap creation critical to maintain ostium patency.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Evidence
content: Mitomycin C (MMC) Efficacy: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) confirm intraoperative MMC significantly boosts success rates in primary E-DCR and revision External DCR by suppressing fibroblast proliferation at the osteotomy margin.

Transcanalicular Diode Laser DCR: Emerging micro-invasive technique using 810nm/980nm laser fibers. Lower long-term success rates (~75-80%) compared to conventional Ext-DCR, but shorter operative time and zero skin scar.
Powered Endoscopic DCR: Utilization of high-speed powered micro-drills and microdebriders drastically reduces intranasal tissue trauma and yields success rates equal to External DCR (>92%).

Non-Stenting Trends: Recent meta-analyses show mucosal flap-to-flap suture anastomosis without silicone stenting has equivalent patency rates in uncomplicated primary Ext-DCR, avoiding stent-related granuloma formation.
